0.label: bust_holding_small_disc
0.description: The right-hand vignette on the mount: a face with round eyes and a square mouth above two arms bent to bring both fists to the chest, a small disc or bead between them, on a hatched ground.
0.iconography: A devotee holding a small round object — a kola nut, an ikin palm nut or a bead — to the chest. It is the figure at the foot of the 48 cm tray KBA_17556, redrawn the right way up.

1.label: face_in_triangular_hood
1.description: The left-hand vignette: a face with eyes, nose and banded mouth set inside a tall pointed triangle with hatched sides, on a hatched ground.
1.iconography: The Ẹ̀ṣù (ojú ọpọ́n) face from the head of the 48 cm tray KBA_17556, framed by a pointed hood — the same triangle-framed head as the two central leaders of the Ado-Ekiti door (EBA-Div_00303 #23, #34).

panel.title: Mount sheet: 'two faces from an Ifá board'
panel.object_type: archive mount sheet with two copied drawings
panel.summary: An album page with an insert of two pen drawings, captioned in German 'Yoruba — 2 faces from an Ifá board' and 'copy of a drawing from the small picture archive'. They are the head and foot figures of the 48 cm tray drawn on KBA_17556.

register_readings.reading: Two excerpted faces side by side: a hooded face and a bust holding a disc.

panel.composition: Two details lifted from one tray — its head and its foot — and set side by side for comparison.
panel.narrative: The sheet shows the archive's own method: pulling the key figures off an object to compare them, much as this project does. The two chosen are the ones that orient the tray: Ẹ̀ṣù's hooded face at the head and a devotee holding a disc at the foot. The hood links tray imagery to the Ado-Ekiti door's triangle-headed leaders.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral; methodologically interesting as an early 'motif extraction'.
uncertainties: A copy of a copy: the drawings are two steps from the carving.
